title: Basic Subjunctive
description: Use the present subjunctive in fixed expressions: wishes, hopes, and Ojalá.

vocabulary.source: I go / you go (subjunctive of ir)

grammar.title: Present Subjunctive in Fixed Expressions
grammar.content:
The subjunctive (subjuntivo) is a mood used to express wishes, doubts, emotions, and hypothetical situations. At A2.1, you'll mainly encounter it in fixed expressions — set phrases where the subjunctive is mandatory.

Wishes and blessings:
- ¡Que tengas un buen día! = Have a good day!
- ¡Que te vaya bien! = Good luck! (literally: may it go well for you)
- ¡Que descanses! = Rest well!

With querer/esperar + que (when the subject changes):
- Quiero que seas feliz. = I want you to be happy.
- Espero que llueva. = I hope it rains.

Common fixed expressions:
- Ojalá (que)... = I hope that... / God willing...
- Es importante que... = It's important that...
- Mejor que... = Better if...

The present subjunctive yo form is built by taking the yo present indicative form and switching the ending: -o → -e for -AR, -o → -a for -ER/-IR:
- hablar → hablo → hable
- comer → como → coma
- vivir → vivo → viva
examples: ¡Que tengas un excelente día! (Have an excellent day!)
Ojalá llueva mañana. (I hope it rains tomorrow.)
Quiero que tú vengas a mi fiesta. (I want you to come to my party.)
Espero que esté bien. (I hope he/she is okay.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian uses a similar 'optative' mood for wishes: 'Să ai o zi bună!' = '¡Que tengas un buen día!' The 'să' particle marks the subjunctive optative. This makes the Spanish subjunctive much more natural for Romanian speakers than for English speakers.

exercises.question: Which of these uses the subjunctive correctly?
exercises.explanation: 'Ojalá llueva mañana' uses the subjunctive correctly. 'Ojalá' always triggers the subjunctive.

exercises.question: Complete: '¡Que tengas ____ día!' (Have a ____ day!) — subjunctive wish for someone.
exercises.explanation: '¡Que tengas un buen día!' uses the subjunctive 'tengas' (from tener) after 'que'.

exercises.question: What is the subjunctive yo form of 'tener'?
exercises.explanation: 'Tenga' is the present subjunctive yo form: take the yo indicative (tengo), drop the -o, add -a for -ER verbs.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Espero que ____ (estar) bien.' (I hope he/she is okay.)
exercises.explanation: 'Esté' is the subjunctive of estar for él/ella/usted: take yo present (estoy), drop -o, add -e: esté.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Quiero que ____ (you) ____ (come) a mi fiesta.' (I want you to come to my party.)
exercises.explanation: 'Vengas' is the subjunctive of venir for tú. Irregular: venir → vengo → vengas.

exercises.question: What triggers the subjunctive after 'ojalá'?
exercises.explanation: 'Ojalá' always triggers the subjunctive: Ojalá llueva, Ojalá venga, etc.
